Z_00101_2.desc: A chainring-style toothed plate with a six-arm web carrying alternating rounded-triangular windows and round holes; the center is a splined through bore instead of a plain hole, and the outer teeth are relieved on one side to give a single-sided tooth profile.

Z_00101_0.desc: A constant-thickness flat disc forming an external spur gear: roughly thirty teeth on the outer rim, an integral five-spoke web running to the center, five large rounded through windows equally spaced between the spokes, and one small central through bore, with every cutout and tooth root filleted.

Z_00013_1.desc: Low-profile square-format carrier of the same family with no full rim: a flat plate stiffened by a sparse underside rib lattice and four raised corner bumpers, presenting a dense six-by-eight field of smaller round-cornered square through-pockets. Two oblong finger slots pierce one long edge, and two moulded datum holes at opposite corners provide stacking registration.

Z_00013_0.desc: Thin rectangular moulded tray built from a flat base panel with an integral low perimeter rim and generously rounded outer corners; one short edge carries a small relieved tab-and-slot detail. The interior field holds a four-by-five array of twenty identical square pockets with filleted corners, separated by uniform thin webs and leaving a blank margin along one side for handling.

Z_00013_2.desc: Deeper open-cassette variant of the same carrier family: a rectangular shell with tall continuous side walls and a reinforced rim, its floor broken by a coarse three-by-four pattern of large rectangular windows with lead-in chamfers. Integral pads and transverse crush ribs on the underside, external stacking lugs on the long walls, and a latch recess at one end let several trays nest and lock.

Z_00071_0.desc: A flat rectangular egg-crate grid built from two perpendicular groups of identical thin strips: five strips run one way and three strips cross them at right angles. Every intersection is a half-lap joint, with a single straight slot cut from the top edge of one group and from the bottom edge of the other, sized to the strip thickness so the assembly slides together and holds by friction. Strips share one constant height and thickness, the cells are open and square, the outer edges are plain with no separate frame, and there are no holes, bosses, or fillets beyond small slot-mouth clearances.

Z_00000_2.part_family: thin-walled molded tray with a grid of circular wells
Z_00000_2.desc: A low-profile carrier plate variant: near-square border with an internal four-by-four array of counterbored blind pockets, every pocket centered on a raised locating boss and tied together by thin molded ribs. Two elongated handling slots pierce one edge, four reinforced holes at the corners share a single bolt circle, and the flat back uses snap-on feet instead of molded ribs.

Z_00000_0.part_family: thin-walled molded tray with a grid of circular wells
Z_00000_0.desc: A shallow rectangular molded pocket tray: a flat deck carries a five-by-four grid of twenty round wells with small lip fillets, enclosed by a continuous raised perimeter rim. Four through-holes sit on a large bolt circle, with additional small through-holes on a secondary circle; the underside is a thin shell broken by short integral stiffening ribs/feet and generous edge rounds.

Z_00000_1.part_family: thin-walled molded tray with a grid of circular wells
Z_00000_1.desc: A deeper compartmented organizer tray of the same family: a wide flanged rectangular rim with stacking ledge and corner mounting lugs surrounds a six-by-three field of large round cups flanked by rows of rectangular recesses. Cross-ribs run beneath the deck, each cup bottom is a blind dimple with a small drain boss, and the rim carries slotted holes rather than a bolt-circle pattern.

Z_00026_2.part_family: thin moulded rectangular display bezel frame
Z_00026_2.desc: An open C-shaped retaining frame rather than a closed ring: three sides form a thin capturing lip while the fourth side is left open for sliding a panel in. The closed corner is reinforced by a gusset rib and two threaded inserts, the opposite long side has a row of evenly spaced ventilation slots plus a pair of flexible latch fingers, and every exposed edge uses one small uniform chamfer with no corner radii.

Z_00026_1.part_family: thin moulded rectangular display bezel frame
Z_00026_1.desc: A deeper rectangular bezel whose ring is split into two stepped levels: a narrow outer ledge for adhesive and a recessed inner shelf that supports a glass panel. Four moulded snap hooks project from the back of the long sides, screw bosses stand at the corners, and a continuous sealing groove runs just inside the outer edge; the front face is chamfered only on the outer rim and the internal corners are generously filleted.

Z_00026_0.part_family: thin moulded rectangular display bezel frame
Z_00026_0.desc: A low-profile closed rectangular ring moulded as one thin shell around a single large central window. The flat web carries a repeating pattern of shallow blind pockets along all four inner edges—long recesses on the short sides and smaller recesses plus tiny slots on the long sides—while the outer corners use mixed radii. Both faces have perimeter chamfers, the outside wall is slightly drafted, and the back face carries a pair of small raised locating pads.

Z_00088_0.desc: One slender uniform-thickness sheet-metal strip with a straight rectangular web and a short continuous lip folded along one long edge, giving a narrow open angle section. It has two small through holes near opposite ends and a small rounded corner at one tip, with no slots, ribs, bosses, or repeated pattern.

Z_00088_1.desc: A wider same-family retainer formed as a shallow channel: a flat center web with both long edges turned into short parallel flanges. It carries three round mounting holes along the web and a pair of elongated slots toward one end, with plain square ends and small corner fillets.

Z_00088_2.desc: A compact offset spring-clip strip bent into a stepped profile with two opposed flanges joined by a narrow web and a curled latch tab at one end. It mixes one obround adjustment slot, two punched holes on the opposite flange, and a single small dimple, leaving the edges otherwise plain.

Z_00078_2.part_family: T-slot aluminum extrusion for modular machine framing
Z_00078_2.desc: Wide heavy-duty framing extrusion with twin T-slots on the top face and single slots on both sides and the bottom. Thick outer walls enclose two internal chambers separated by webs with three longitudinal screw bores, all slot lips chamfered for nut insertion, and both ends faced flat for bracket mounting.

Z_00078_1.part_family: T-slot aluminum extrusion for modular machine framing
Z_00078_1.desc: Long, slim single-slot extrusion with one T-slot on each of two opposite faces and a shallow open central cavity containing a single pilot bore for self-tapping screws. Two outer corners are rounded, the remaining edges are chamfered, and one end is cross-drilled and tapped to accept a hidden corner connector.

Z_00075_0.part_family: open split retaining ring (C-clip) of uniform section
Z_00075_0.desc: A single C-shaped open ring formed from constant square-section metal strip, with smooth concentric inner and outer cylindrical faces and equal axial thickness. The loop closes most of a circle and stops at a bottom gap; both free ends are cut on an angle to make small chamfered tip faces, and there are no holes, ribs, or bosses beyond the central through opening.

Z_00075_2.part_family: open split retaining ring (C-clip) of uniform section
Z_00075_2.desc: A single-turn round-wire spring retaining ring that is slightly oval in the free state rather than truly circular. Its two ends are bent into opposed inward-facing hook eyes that pass the gap, the outer crest carries a shallow coined flat, and one short radial prong projects outward near mid-arc for orientation.

Z_00075_1.part_family: open split retaining ring (C-clip) of uniform section
Z_00075_1.desc: A flat stamped external snap ring: a thin constant-thickness annular C-plate whose radial width is much greater than its axial thickness. The gap is flanked by two opposed lug ears, each pierced with one round plier hole, with a small locating notch on the inner edge and gently rounded, deburred end corners.

Z_00027_2.part_family: slender turned contact/test-probe pin with forked tip and cross-hole
Z_00027_2.desc: A double-ended variant: one continuous slender rod carrying a mirror-image hooked fork at each tip, an enlarged central locating collar midway along the shank, a transverse through-hole adjacent to each fork, chamfers on all prong edges, and a shallow longitudinal flat milled on the shank as an anti-rotation key; seating is by the collar, with no threaded features.

Z_00027_0.part_family: slender turned contact/test-probe pin with forked tip and cross-hole
Z_00027_0.desc: One monolithic slim round shaft of constant small diameter forms the body, with a plain cylindrical tail at one end and a short machined working head at the other. The head is necked and split into two opposed hooked prongs (a narrow bifurcated/arrow profile), pierced by a single small transverse through-hole, and break-edged with eight larger chamfers, four smaller chamfers and four small corner radii; there are no threads, ribs, bosses or separate panels.

Z_00027_1.part_family: slender turned contact/test-probe pin with forked tip and cross-hole
Z_00027_1.desc: Same pin family but as a spring-loaded probe plunger: a slim round shank with a single solid rounded/conical contact nose instead of a fork, a rear annular spring seat and crimp collar, one cross-drilled retention hole just behind the nose, only a pair of lead-in chamfers, and a solder slot in the tail rather than a plain end.

Z_00012_0.part_family: flanged internally splined coupling hub with press-fit toothed insert
Z_00012_0.desc: Axisymmetric turned-metal hub: a thin circular mounting flange is joined to a short cylindrical sleeve, and a separate ring carrying external axial ribs is pressed into the sleeve bore; the ring bore has continuous internal spline teeth along its length and terminates in a shaped polygonal through-hole, with a thin annular wall between spline roots and the sleeve OD, small pilot shoulders on the flange face, and a retaining lip at the insert end.

Z_00012_2.part_family: flanged internally splined coupling hub with press-fit toothed insert
Z_00012_2.desc: Compact bolted flanged bushing: a thicker dished flange carries a bolt circle of through holes and a central locating recess, the short sleeve holds a single internal spline finished by a longitudinal keyway slot in its through-bore, an external circlip groove sits near the sleeve mouth, and one tapped radial set-screw boss protrudes from the barrel wall.

Z_00012_1.part_family: flanged internally splined coupling hub with press-fit toothed insert
Z_00012_1.desc: Long stepped spline coupling: a two-diameter barrel with external gear teeth on the large end replaces the flange, two internal spline rows are separated by an internal circlip groove, a smooth counterbore pilots the mating shaft, one end is internally chamfered for lead-in, and several small radial oil holes break through the wall between the spline rows.

Z_00067_2.desc: L-shaped sheet-metal angle bracket with a long vertical leg and a short horizontal foot, both punched before forming. The vertical leg has a column of three countersunk holes plus one keyhole slot at its free end, the foot carries two tapped-hole bosses formed as small extrusions, and a single hemmed edge stiffens the top of the vertical leg.

Z_00067_1.desc: Bent sheet-metal mounting clip formed into a U-channel from one blank, with two parallel side legs joined by a flat base web. The base carries two clearance holes for fasteners, each leg has one elongated adjustment slot, and a small formed dimple near one end acts as a detent; edges are sheared with modest bend radii at the two folds.

Z_00067_0.desc: Single strip of uniform thin sheet metal bent into a shallow Z / ramp profile: a short-upright end tab carries a small through hole, the inclined central web holds one larger through hole near the top bend and a small punched rectangular slot mid-slope, and the strip ends in a low flat foot flange. All holes and the slot are punched through the sheet in the flat pattern, with simple bend radii at the fold lines and plain sheared edges.

Z_00054_2.desc: A shorter, stockier chevron prism with the peak inverted into a V-groove that runs the full length of the top, an integral rectangular boss on the base, and three blind pockets milled in a row into the back face. All external corners are filleted rather than sharp, giving a softened version of the same profiled-block concept.

Z_00054_0.desc: One straight, constant-depth solid bar whose end face is cut to an arrowhead silhouette: a low rectangular heel, a single rising ramp to an apex, a shallow V-notch, then a final rise to a tall vertical trailing edge. The long body stays a plain rectangular prism, so the front and top views read as rectangles crossed by a few sharp vertical break lines (solid where the peak and notch project, dashed where hidden). Flat faces only, sharp external corners, and no holes, slots, ribs, bosses or fillets.

Z_00054_1.desc: A longer solid extrusion of the same family whose end profile carries two symmetric triangular teeth separated by a deeper central V, with a full-length rectangular base and two cross-depth through-holes near the heel for mounting. The long edges get a small uniform chamfer, but the body remains a single prismatic block with no pockets.

Z_00089_1.desc: Tall single-bay version of the same strip grille: two full-length side rails bridged by one regular row of horizontal rungs, with a formed mounting flange along the bottom edge and a pair of slotted hanging hooks at the top. Small pressed dimples between rungs stiffen mid-span, and there are no side standoff tabs.

Z_00089_0.desc: Rectangular open lattice assembled from thin flat metal strip: several upright stiles are tied by many evenly spaced horizontal rungs into adjacent ladder bays across a squat oblong outline. Short mounting feet sit on the top edge, a column of small rectangular standoff tabs projects from one side edge at a few heights for clipping to a rail or a mating panel, and a shallow bent foot at the base forms a standoff; crossings are spot-joined with essentially square edges and no modelled fillets.

Z_00082_0.desc: Thin uniform sheet plate whose solid central hub is integrally joined to six identical narrow arms set in a regular hexagonal radial pattern; each arm ends in a raised circular eye boss carrying a through-hole with a countersunk seat on one face, all six holes sharing a common bolt circle with filleted arm-to-boss transitions and an open lattice between arms.

Z_00082_2.desc: Annular eight-spoke variant built as a center ring (large central opening) linked by eight short spokes to circular end pads; the pads alternate between tapped blind bosses on one face and clevis-like paired ears with a cross-hole on others, and the outer edge is scalloped between pads with thin radial gussets tying spokes to the ring.

Z_00082_1.desc: Four-arm version of the same family arranged as an X about a central hub that has a large through-bore with a single keyway and a rear pilot recess; each tapered arm is pressed with an embossed stiffening rib and terminates in a turned-up lug pierced by an elongated slot, with small lightening holes in the hub web.

Z_00016_0.desc: A single straight constant-cross-section toothed bar: a slender solid rail with dense fine teeth running lengthwise on the working faces, rounded roots, tips and edge fillets, and one clean axial through bore; the ends are plain square cuts with no separate joints, bosses, or side branches.

Z_00016_2.desc: A wider multi-track spline strip formed as one extrusion: parallel toothed tracks are separated by shallow guide grooves, one edge carries an integral locating rib, the opposite edge has small clearance slots and cross holes, and both ends are counterbored for pins; fillets are fuller on loaded flanks and smaller on non-contact edges.

Z_00016_1.desc: A curved rack segment of the same family, with teeth only on the inner arc, a smooth outer back, two integral end lugs with slotted mounting holes, and a relieved central web instead of a through bore; tooth engagement blends into plain runout pads at both ends.

Z_00050_2.desc: A flat anchor plate of constant thickness built from a broad roughly rectangular body with one projecting ear on the longer side. The body carries a central obround slot and a rectangular cluster of four small mounting holes, the ear carries a single large through bore, one corner holds a small locating notch, and the outer edges mix small chamfers and rounded corners while remaining one flat lamina.

Z_00050_1.desc: A flat profiled lever plate of uniform thickness with a straight, slightly tapered web joining two circular end bosses, each boss carrying one large pivot bore. The web is opened with two round lightening holes and a line of three small clearance holes near one edge, the perimeter is fully rounded with generous fillets at the boss-to-web transitions, and the part is entirely planar with no slots or formed features.

Z_00111_1.desc: A thin rectangular sheet-metal bezel with a continuous raised outer rim and a honeycomb rib lattice spanning a single wide window. The rim carries six clearance holes on one bolt circle, two oblong tool slots, and a pair of folded side flanges for stiffness, with small round fillets wherever the ribs meet the rim.

Z_00001_2.desc: Rectangular low-profile vent cover in the same protective-grille family, using an oval outer rim, two opposed mounting ears, transverse louver bars over a central opening, and small locator bosses on the back face rather than a concentric-ring pattern.

Z_00001_0.desc: Single-piece shallow square guard plate with rounded corner radii and a central circular protective grille; concentric ring ribs are joined by radial and diagonal spokes to a small center hub, and the flat rim carries many small rounded through-features for airflow and fastening clearance.

Z_00002_2.part_family: flat radial spider hub with end socket cups
Z_00002_2.desc: Two-arm bar coupler of the same family: an elongated thin web with a central collar and through hole, carrying one raised square recessed socket at each opposite end. Shallow lightening slots pierce each arm web, there are no ribs on the cup walls, and the few sharp edges are eased with minimal rounds.

Z_00002_1.part_family: flat radial spider hub with end socket cups
Z_00002_1.desc: Cross-shaped flat hub with a central through-bored boss and four radial arms at right angles, each arm ending in a closed circular counterbored pad instead of an open cup. Small triangular gusset ribs reinforce the arm roots, the edge is a uniform plate thickness, and only the outer corners are filleted.

Z_00002_0.part_family: flat radial spider hub with end socket cups
Z_00002_0.desc: Thin tri-lobed plate built around a central annular collar with a through bore; three short spokes at equal angles connect the collar to three raised open hexagonal cups, each cup having a recessed hexagonal cavity and a rolled outer rim. Every outer corner, cup lip and spoke root is broken by many small rounds, and the face is stepped between a thicker perimeter ring and a thinner inner floor.

Z_00072_2.desc: Same family as a thin-wall open-top enclosure half: a shallow tray with a peripheral locating lip, one long sidewall pierced by an evenly spaced line of circular connector cutouts while the opposite wall is blank with standoff bosses. Interior ribs divide the cavity into pockets, a single row of alignment holes runs beside an elongated central keying slot, and small fillets reinforce the rib-to-wall junctions.

Z_00072_0.desc: Elongated metal block with an inverted-channel cross section: a thick top deck ties two downward side legs and leaves a continuous open cavity beneath. The deck carries a dense regular grid of small through holes in repeated rows, broken by a central rectangular polarizing slot and by scattered depth-limited or counterbored holes; two small groups of holes sit on circular bolt patterns, the end faces add a transverse slot and extra through holes, and a thin upright flange portion is relieved with stacked rectangular windows and stepped edges. Corners are filleted inside and lightly chamfered outside.
